svg.title: Synchrotron ring and drift tubes
svg.desc: (a) A synchrotron: a ring of evenly spaced accelerating tubes around a circular beam path. (b) A proton between two tubes is pushed forward by the electric field E from the positive tube behind it toward the negative tube ahead. (c) After the proton enters the tube and coasts through it, the voltages reverse, so the field in the next gap again pushes it forward. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: A synchrotron raises its magnetic field as momentum increases
Fixed R, with relativistic p = mc√(γ² − 1). The field follows p; revolution frequency follows v. A
continuous ramp approximates many RF kicks; the gold marker locates an RF cavity.
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
